conviction_note: Event confirmed (Q1 trading update, 15 Oct 2026, Dunelm's updates go out at 07:00). The softer first six weeks of FY27 and a flat FY27 adjusted PBT guide (£211m, which is also the company-compiled consensus from 14 analysts) were published on 8 Sep, so the only new items are the Q1 sales number against a +6.2% comp and whether the guide is reiterated. Findings are small and offset: the CEO and the Chair bought shares and DFS reported orders in line with its plan, against a weak September macro proxy. The sum is +0.4 and the scaled number (2*0.53-1)*4.5 = +0.27. abs_move is kept at 4.5 because a guide change on this name has moved it 14-20%, even though a reiteration is the likelier outcome.

findings.finding: Q1 FY27 is up against the hardest comp of FY26 (+6.2% total sales, +2.2% LFL) and the company has already said the first six of its 13 weeks were 'significantly softer'. The headline Q1 sales number will probably be flat to negative and the new information is only its size.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 trading updates moved -0.87% (Oct 2023), +0.25% (Oct 2024) and -0.44% (Oct 2025). Sales-led trading updates without a guidance change have moved under 1% at Q1.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the weak start was disclosed and the stock fell 14.3% that day. What is not priced is the exact Q1 number. If the market expected a worse print the stock would not have rebounded 9% off the low, so the residual risk is that a negative headline against the +6.2% comp reads badly in the wire copy.
findings.independence: The comp numbers are in the same document. Next H1 says warm weather helped clothing, the opposite of homewares (https://www.proactiveinvestors.com/companies/news/1098670/next-raises-profit-guidance-after-stronger-than-expected-first-half-1098670.html).

findings.finding: Peers reporting since Dunelm spoke point to a soft but stable market. DFS (FY from late June, as at Dunelm) said order intake in the first 12 weeks of FY27 was -2.5%, 'in line with our expectations notwithstanding extreme weather', and reiterated moderate FY27 profit growth in line with consensus (24 Sep). Wickes said Q3 retail LFL has stepped up to mid-single-digit growth (15 Sep).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured Dunelm reaction to peer read-across. Dunelm's own guidance changes moved it -19.5% (Jan 2026 profit trim) and -14.3% (Sep 2026 flat guide).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: DFS is public, and Dunelm rose from 758p (18 Sep) to about 800p after it. If the market had read 'sector in line, no further weather damage' as settled, Dunelm would be re-rating rather than trading 10% below its pre-prelims price. The read-across to a reiterated Dunelm guide is an inference. DFS is upholstery and big-ticket, while Dunelm is mostly smaller-ticket homewares.
findings.independence: Wickes interims, Q3 to date, a separate document: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/wickes-group--wix/wickes-group-plc-interim-results-2026/9771583

findings.finding: The CEO bought 7,781 shares at 792.67p on 22 Sep 2026, four days before the Q1 period ended (13 weeks from 28 Jun) and with most of the quarter's trading visible to her. The Chair (10,000 at 732.29p, 9 Sep) and three NEDs also bought after the prelims. This makes a profit-guide cut on 15 Oct less likely.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior instance measured. The relevant line is guidance, where Dunelm has moved -14% to -20% on cuts and resets.
findings.why_not_priced: The purchases are public but small (£62k from the CEO, £73k from the Chair) and were not reported widely; no wire preview ties them to the Q1 update. A CEO cannot lawfully buy while holding inside information, so the purchase implies that Q1 trading on 22 Sep was not materially off the guided path. The 20-day run-up of +6% is consistent with partial recognition, and a fully priced 'no cut' would show a recovery nearer the 880p pre-prelims price. On 28 Sep the CEO sold 47,817 shares at £8.00 to cover tax on LTIP buy-out options, which is not a discretionary sale (https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/dunelm-group--dnlm/director-pdmr-shareholding/9796511).
findings.independence: Chair purchase, separate RNS: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/dunelm-group--dnlm/director-pdmr-shareholding/9764315 ; NED purchases: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/dunelm-group--dnlm/director-pdmr-shareholding/9775756

findings.finding: September consumer data are soft for homewares. BRC-KPMG non-food sales were +0.3% for the five weeks to 3 Oct, after -0.8% in August, when big-ticket furniture declined. BDO's High Street Sales Tracker has homewares LFL at -7.8% for the four weeks to 27 Sep against a +8.2% base. This works against Dunelm's 'better trading following cooler weather' carrying through the quarter's last weeks.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured Dunelm reaction to these series.
findings.why_not_priced: These are public macro series that a 14-analyst name will have seen. They go from the economy to the company only by inference. BDO's homewares line is a narrow, noisy panel: it read -3.0% in July and +20.3% in August, in the weeks Dunelm itself called significantly softer, so it does not track Dunelm. The broad BRC non-food series in September (+0.3%, above its 12-month average of +0.2%) is not weak. Sized small for those reasons.

baseline_tension: The small net-positive findings agree with the mildly positive lean (+0.39) and the +6% 20-day rebound, so a reiteration is partly priced. The negative sizes rest on public proxies and the positive ones on inference, which is why p_up is held near 50.
language_note: The domestic RNS channel (Investegate) carried the PDMR purchase notices: the CEO on 22 Sep at 792.67p, the Chair and three NEDs after the prelims. No English wire coverage tied them to the Q1 update.

Dunelm's own IR site carries a company-compiled consensus (14 analysts, FY27 adj PBT £211m, revenue £1,897m, 18 Sep). This sets the bar more firmly than the wire snippets, which cite only individual brokers.
The domestic trade press and the BDO tracker carried the September homewares data (-7.8% LFL). The English wire copy reported only headline BRC numbers.
lessons_applied: 'A finding about a number the market has already been told is worth 0': the Q1-comp/weak-start finding moved toward 0, from -0.3 to -0.2, because the softness was disclosed on 8 Sep.
'A narrow proxy loses to a broad series': the September macro finding went from -0.4 to -0.2. BDO homewares contradicts its own August reading and the broad BRC non-food series is not weak.

'Let the reaction history move p_up, not abs_move_pct': abs_move stays at 4.5 despite small past Q1 reactions, because guide changes on this name moved it 14-20%. p_up went from 52 to 53 once the negatives were cut.
